title: Color grading engine: scopes, probes and machine-readable measurement
base: codex/color-grading-cg0-cg2 77722bb0 (PR #77, CG0-CG2), later merged with its tip 0811876e (which merges main 51ffe62a, PR #76)
visualAcceptance: none: measurement tooling only; the scope images were looked at by the agent as a sanity check, which is not acceptance

delivered.colorScience: packages/color-science/src/scopes.ts: luma waveform, RGB parade, BT.709 vectorscope, RGB/luma/hue/saturation histograms, CIE 1931 xy, SDR false color, exposure zones (ported from chroma-node scopeAnalysis.ts b804dc0); new: 123-degree skin-tone line, pixel coordinates (encoded, linear, HSL, CIELAB, OKLab), HSL qualifier suggestions
delivered.reuse: comp color-stats' measureColorFrames is now a wrapper over colorStatisticsAccumulator (same summation order); comp scopes embeds its ColorStatistics unchanged and the CGA color integration tests (21) pass

commands.comp scopes: evenly sampled frames or --frame-range start:end, optional --region; report still-shift-color-scopes-1 validated by a zod schema; optional waveform/parade/vectorscope/CIE PNGs
commands.comp probe: one layer's effect stack rendered stage by stage in the pinned browser; point (with radius) or region; coordinates and qualifier suggestion; other layers disabled by default
commands.comp grade diff: two clips of one size: statistics, changes, split still, contact sheet

provenancePortChanges: bins are floor(v * bins) clamped (chroma-node scaled by bins - 1, so the last bin held a single value)
the hue histogram skips achromatic pixels (chroma-node counted greys as hue 0, red)
neutral luma is exact (the Rec.709 weights sum to 0.9999999999999999 in float64, which moved exact zone boundaries)
delivered.deferred: scope types beyond the measured set (YCbCr/YRGB parades, HDR waveform, CIE 1976) and probe coordinates at arbitrary graph nodes (CG9) are not built; the chroma-node HDR false-color ranges wait for CG7/CG8

checks.check: Statistics on CG0 synthetic fixtures match analytically known values
checks.evidence: gray ramp waveform is the diagonal (32 per column) and its luma histogram flat; RGB ramp parades trace their own band; every hue-sweep pixel's hue is its column within 0.6 degrees; saturation-sweep saturation is x/255 within byte rounding; BT.709 primaries at their analytic Cb/Cr (red at Cr 0.5, 103 degrees); skin tones within 15 degrees of the skin line; the chart's neutrals at D65 xy within 1e-4; false-color and exposure-zone counts on the ramp equal the class bounds; pixel coordinates of white, 18% grey and red

checks.check: Scope JSON is byte-stable across reruns and validated by a schema
checks.evidence: two runs of comp scopes on the CG0 moving clip (frames 10:14, with images) give byte-identical JSON and identical PNG hashes; every report is parsed by ColorScopesReportSchema before it is returned, and the test parses the CLI output with it

checks.check: Probe before/after values match the float64 reference for a graded pixel
checks.evidence: CG0 chart with grade.primary then grade.cdl, probed on Canvas at a patch: the input stage equals the source bytes, the stage after grade.primary equals floatGradeBytes of that operator and the stage after grade.cdl equals the two-operator run, exactly

checks.check: Works on a native-video frame range within the existing media memory limits; over-budget requests fail with a clear diagnostic
checks.evidence: frames decode in batches of floor(mediaLimits.decodedFrameBytes / frame bytes); with a three-frame budget an 8-frame range is measured in batches of 3 with a report identical to the unbatched one; a frame over the limit fails with comp-scope-limit before decoding; a range outside the clip fails with comp-scope-range; a region outside the frame fails

checks.check: Documented in the CLI README and generated reference
checks.evidence: CLI README 'Color measurement: scopes, probe and grade diff' and command table row; the generated skill names the commands (the composition reference itself documents composition fields, not CLI commands)

failedRunsAndReruns: The scope module was written before its unit tests (not failing-first); the tests were written next and one failed on a real defect, fixed: neutral luma lost an ulp to the weights' float sum and put code 51 in exposure zone 1 instead of 2.

CLI integration tests were written before the commands and failed first with comp-program-command (unknown composition command scopes / probe / grade); the module-level batching test passed from the start because the module existed.

One integration test expected the background hue peak in the 80-90 degree bin; the background's hue is exactly 80 degrees, so noise and 4:2:0 chroma split it between bins 7 and 8. The test now checks the two bins together (> 0.6) and no skin pixels.
A single compound shell command for the accumulator refactor was refused by the worktree guard; the edit was redone with the editor.
pnpm install rewrote pnpm-lock.yaml's quoting again; Prettier restored it, leaving only the new dependency entry.
schema:check flagged the native appearance closure after the renderer's color-science import gained the scope module; regenerated (identity only).
workspace: CG3 runs in its own worktree (.claude/worktrees/color-grading-cg3) at the owner's choice, because the PR #77 review session was committing in the CG0-CG2 worktree.

checkFast: run 1 failed format:check on one line of composition-color-scopes.ts (from a sed type fix); formatted in its own commit
verification.integration: composition-scopes, composition-color (CGA), composition-color-cli: 3 files, 32 tests passed

browser.color-grading-cg2: passed after merging the PR #77 tip (88 parity rows: Canvas 0, WebGL2 <= 1)

verification.notRunHere: composition-baselines and composition-effects: CG3 changes no renderer source; the merged main/PR #77 renderer changes were verified on their own branches

notRun: pnpm check, full pnpm test, runtime tier, release checks
next: Report to the owner. Then CG4 (curves and tonal-range tools) and CG5 (LUT and CDL interchange), which can run in parallel after CG2.
